page: Amazon Web Services m7a.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors running at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 system provides 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 384.0 GB of high-frequency 5 GHz DDR5 memory. This delivers a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache configurations alongside AVX-512 vector support. The instance operates without bundled local NVMe storage and features a baseline network throughput of 38 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier compute and memory throughput. Multi-core operations scale linearly due to the dedicated 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation, placing stress-ng multi-core (293,589.22), Geekbench multi-core (22,335.0), and PassMark CPU score (106,240.69) within the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Memory-intensive cached reads achieve 11,726.96 GB/sec, while uncached reads register at 328.46 GB/sec. Application-level metrics show 168.46 million Redis SET operations per second and 69.28 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based LLM inference handles 5,460.99 prompt tokens per second on compact 135M parameter models and 48.65 generation tokens per second on 7B models.

The absence of internal physical disks requires reliance on networked block storage, shifting I/O economics toward external storage architecture. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high core density and dedicated execution threads minimize resource contention, maximizing CPU throughput per dollar in heavily threaded environments. The m7a.24xlarge is well positioned for enterprise web fleets, distributed in-memory caching tiers, large-scale CI/CD build farms, and batch data transformation workloads that demand sustained CPU capacity with balanced memory allocations.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.24xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with a 96-core AMD EPYC 9R14 processor at 3.7 GHz, delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per physical core. Built on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 extensions, it incorporates 384.0 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB per core. The server includes no local disk storage, has zero GPUs, and delivers 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic testing places its multi-threaded processing, compilation speed, and Redis operations in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Given its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration and high thread density, the instance is engineered for distributed application servers, in-memory key-value databases, continuous integration build jobs, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
